question: How can the same input-conditioned retrieval prior and passage-conditioned generator yield different sequence probabilities when document marginalization occurs outside versus inside token multiplication?
element_groups: Passage corpus, fixed document encoder/vector index, trainable query encoder, MIPS/top-K and input-conditioned document prior.
Original x plus one candidate passage; shared generator parameters within each fitted model, prefix condition and token likelihood.
Alternative sequence-level versus token-level document sums with explicit index sets and autoregressive prefixes.
Training pairs and marginal NLL, Adam query/generator update; independent decoding alternatives and task-specific settings.

source_relations.meaning: Input-conditioned retrieval and one-passage generator context; Sequence sums document after token products, Token sums within each token transition.
Adam trains query encoder and generator; document encoder/index fixed; fine-tuning supervision differs from DPR initialization.
Candidate-document Thorough/Fast scores and Token mixture decoding; open-domain QA greedy both, Open-MSMarco/Jeopardy beam4, testK task-specific.

source_relations.location: mainp5 Section3.4 vs supplementp2 AppendixE; supplementpp2–3G
source_relations.meaning: FEVER implementation qualification and parameter/dimension source tension kept explicit.

visual_design: A separates query and fixed corpus/index. B gives one candidate context and prefix/parameter ownership. C places noncommuting sums/products in side-by-side alternatives. D separates training updates from inference decoding, with shared task settings below both branches. Semantic aliases and local shorthand are defined; full caption is part of delivery.
transferable_rules: Name each aggregation axis and conditional set before arranging operations; moving a sum across a product changes latent-variable meaning.
Different token-level latent-document contributions do not by themselves establish new query-dependent retrieval or hard document selection.
Keep document probability weight distinct from the text fed into the generator; each retrieved passage context uses within-model shared parameters.
Separate fine-tuning update ownership from supervised initialization; task-specific decoder settings qualify generic algorithm boxes.

unknowns.assessment: The source gives a proportional exponential prior, top-K truncation and approximate marginalization. It does not resolve the exact code normalization universe; no code was read or run.

Raw-text storage layout, lookup schema, tokenizer, separators, concatenation order and truncation behavior are not established by these sources. Logical input/passages and stored vectors are established.

Appendix E establishes regeneration, final-hidden-state classification and document marginalization. It does not specify every training/inference operation, loss interaction, class-token implementation or exact extraction of that hidden state in the supplied text. No reconciliation by invented code behavior is warranted.

The reported 626M trainable wording conflicts with its own fixed-document-encoder qualification. The printed 728 index dimension is retained as source wording, without claiming it is correct or replacing it with another value. Omitting totals/dimensions while showing fixed/update roles is adequate.
Main and appendix specify algorithmic approximations and some settings. Actual caching, retrieval-call counts, numerical implementation and unmentioned beam hyperparameters have not been verified.
Section 4.3 prose says 17 percent for both factual whereas Table 4 says 11.7 percent for Both good. This review does not adjudicate that discrepancy; no number from it enters the method draft.
